slides.name: 1 · Your AI-ready future

params.text: Preparing for careers in an AI-transformed world

slides.notes:
AI AWARENESS DAY 2026 · Starter 5 · Principle: FUTURE · 5 minutes

LEARNING OBJECTIVES
· Understand how AI is changing the job market
· Identify skills that will remain valuable alongside AI
· Recognise the importance of lifelong learning

TONE — from the teacher pack:
Balance realism with optimism. Changes are coming, but so are opportunities. Emphasise that students have agency here. Avoid specific predictions — the exact jobs of 2035 are genuinely unknowable, and pretending otherwise undermines everything else you say.

slides.name: 2 · Statement · frame

params.text: If AI can do many jobs faster than humans, what skills will make you valuable?
Talk to the person next to you — 60 seconds

slides.notes:
A word cloud rather than a poll: there is no fixed list of right answers, and watching the room converge on "creativity", "empathy" and "communication" without being told is worth more than a slide saying so.

DISCUSSION PROMPTS
→ Which skills do you have that AI cannot replicate?
→ How might your dream job change because of AI?
→ What new skills might you want to develop?

feedback.prompt: One skill that will still matter

slides.name: 3 · 170 million new jobs by 2030 — and 92 million displaced

params.text: 170 million new jobs by 2030 — and 92 million displaced
Net new jobs by 2030 — 170 million created, 92 million displaced
Growth in AI-skilled job postings — faster than other job postings
Core work skills that will change by 2030 — lifelong learning is not optional

params.label: Takeaway
params.text: WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 · PwC 2025

slides.notes:
Lead with the net figure. "170 million new jobs" alone is spin and "92 million displaced" alone is doom — the honest number is +78 million, and students can handle it.

One more from the teacher pack if you want it: professionals with AI skills command up to a 56% salary premium (PwC 2025). Use with care — it motivates some rooms and alienates others.

slides.name: 4 · Six things that stay valuable

params.text: Empathy, emotional intelligence, relationships, ethical judgment.
Original thinking, artistic vision, inventive problem-solving.
Critical analysis, nuanced judgment, handling ambiguity.

slides.notes:
Reveal one at a time, matching them to what the room already said in the word cloud — "somebody said kindness, that is this one". It makes the list theirs rather than yours.

LAB — SlideForge shows 6 cards here; the lab's cards take four a slide, so the rest are in these notes: AI-complementary — Knowing how to work WITH AI. Prompt engineering is a real skill.; Adaptability — Willingness to keep learning throughout your career..

slides.name: 5 · Which jobs change, which jobs grow

params.text: Which jobs change, which jobs grow
AI trainers, ethics officers, prompt engineers

slides.notes:
HIDDEN BY DEFAULT — the teacher pack's first sub-question.

The single most important line is not on the slide, so say it: most jobs will be TRANSFORMED, not destroyed. AI handles parts, humans handle the rest. The left column is tasks, not careers.

Protected: anything needing physical presence, human connection, or creative judgment.

slides.name: 7 · Two words worth knowing

params.text: Understanding, using and critically evaluating AI — how it works, where it fails, and how to use it ethically.
Writing effective instructions for AI systems: being clear, being specific, and giving relevant context.

slides.notes:
Both definitions were in the teacher pack only.

Worth noting that "prompt engineering" may not survive as a job title — the skill will likely be absorbed into ordinary literacy, the way "being good at internet searching" was. The underlying ability to ask a precise question is the durable part.

slides.name: 8 · Building your AI-ready skillset

params.text: Five moves you can start this year
Prompt engineering and AI literacy are valuable now.
The ability to learn new skills is the skill.
Data science, AI ethics, machine learning, AI product design.

slides.notes: Reveal one at a time. If you are short of time, end here.

params.text: The future belongs to those who can work with AI while bringing uniquely human value.

slides.name: 10 · Section · If any of this affected you

params.text: If any of this affected you
You will not be in trouble for asking for help.

slides.notes:
Say this out loud rather than leaving it on the slide.

Your tutor, head of year or safeguarding lead is available to help — name the actual person if you can.

From the teacher pack, the three messages that matter most:
· If you are targeted by deepfake abuse, it is NOT your fault.
· Creating AI-generated intimate images of anyone is illegal.
· You will NOT be in trouble for reporting — we are here to help.

Have the safeguarding details ready to share privately with anyone who comes to you afterwards.
